Palmyra Terrace, NassauThunderballSharks in the pool. Rum on the terrace.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersNassau prawn frittersChopped prawns, capsicum, celery and thyme in a crisp Bahamian fritter batter, with lime and pink sauceHow to make it400g raw prawns, peeled and deveined150g plain flour1 tsp baking powder1/2 tsp salt1 egg125ml milk1/2 green capsicum, finely diced1/2 onion, finely diced1 celery stick, finely diced1 small red chilli, finely chopped1 tsp thyme leaves3 tbsp whole egg mayonnaise2 tbsp tomato sauce1 tsp hot chilli sauce1 lime750ml vegetable oil, for fryingChop the prawns into small pieces.Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt, egg and milk into a thick batter.Stir in the prawns, capsicum, onion, celery, chilli and thyme.Mix the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, chilli sauce and a squeeze of the lime for the dipping sauce.Heat the oil to 180°C in a deep heavy pan.Fry heaped spoonfuls in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through. Drain on paper towel.Serve hot with the dipping sauce and the rest of the lime in wedges.Shrublands health farm cruditésCrisp carrot, cucumber, radish, celery and capsicum sticks with green herb yoghurt dipHow to make it200g Greek yoghurt2 tbsp whole egg mayonnaise1 bunch parsley1 bunch chives1/2 bunch basil1 lemon, juiced1 garlic clovesalt, to taste2 carrots2 Lebanese cucumbers4 celery sticks1 red capsicum1 bunch radishesBlitz the yoghurt, mayonnaise, parsley, chives, basil leaves, lemon juice, garlic and salt until green and smooth.Chill the dip for 30 minutes.Cut the carrots, cucumbers, celery and capsicum into sticks, trim the radishes and crisp in iced water for 10 minutes.Drain well and arrange around the dip.Conch salad with lime and chilliEaten poolside. Don't drop any for the sharks.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsPalmyra grilled lobster tails with Bahamian baked macaroniSplit lobster tails grilled with garlic, lime and paprika butter, with Bahamian baked macaroni and cheeseHow to make it300g macaroni2 eggs375ml tin evaporated milk250g tasty cheese, grated1/2 green capsicum, finely diced1/2 onion, finely dicedcayenne pepper, a pinch1 tsp salt1/4 tsp black pepper20g butter, for the macaroni80g butter, for the garlic butter3 garlic cloves, crushed1 lime1/2 tsp sweet paprika4 raw lobster tails, or 8 Moreton Bay bugs1 tbsp parsley, choppedHeat the oven to 180°C. Cook the macaroni in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says and drain.Whisk the eggs, evaporated milk, 200g of the cheese, the capsicum, onion, cayenne, salt, pepper and melted butter for the macaroni. Stir in the macaroni, tip into a baking dish and top with the rest of the cheese.Bake for 40 minutes until set and golden, then rest for 10 minutes.Melt the butter for the garlic butter with the garlic, the zest and juice of the lime and the paprika.Split the lobster tails lengthways through the shell with a heavy knife and brush the flesh with the garlic butter.Grill flesh side up under a hot grill or on a barbecue for 6 to 8 minutes, basting, until just opaque.Scatter with parsley and serve with the macaroni.Junkanoo stew chicken with peas and riceThe night of the Junkanoo parade Bond runs through in NassauHow to make it1kg chicken thighs, bone in1 onion, sliced1 green capsicum, sliced3 garlic cloves, crushed1 tsp ground allspice4 sprigs of thyme2 tbsp tomato paste2 tbsp brown sugar300g long grain rice400g tin pigeon peas or kidney beans, drained2 ripe plantains or firm bananas3 tbsp vegetable oilMelt the sugar in 1 tbsp oil until dark, then brown the chicken in it.Add the onion, capsicum, garlic, allspice, thyme, tomato paste and 300ml water and simmer covered until tender.Cook the rice with the peas, 600ml water and salt, covered, until tender.Fry the sliced plantain in the rest of the oil and serve with the chicken and rice.SweetsNassau guava duff with rum butter sauceSteamed Bahamian roly-poly swirled with spiced guava, sliced and covered in warm rum butter sauceHow to make it250g plain flour, plus extra for rolling2 tsp baking powdersalt, a pinch2 tbsp caster sugar60g cold butter, diced, plus extra for the paper1 egg125ml milk250g guava paste2 tbsp water1/2 tsp ground cinnamon1/4 tsp ground nutmeg80g butter, for the sauce100g brown sugar80ml thickened cream2 tbsp dark rumRub the cold butter into the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar, then stir in the egg and milk to a soft dough.Roll out on floured baking paper to a 25 x 30cm rectangle.Warm the guava paste with the water, cinnamon and nutmeg until spreadable, then spread over the dough leaving a 2cm border.Roll up from a long side, wrap loosely in buttered baking paper, then foil, and twist the ends.Steam on a rack in a covered pot over simmering water for 75 minutes, topping up the water.For the sauce, melt the butter and brown sugar, stir in the cream and bubble for 2 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the rum.Rest the duff for 5 minutes, unwrap, slice thickly and pour over the sauce.DrinksDisco Volante goombay smashCoconut rum with pineapple, orange and lime over ice, dark rum floated on topHow to make it120ml coconut rum360ml pineapple juice60ml orange juice30ml lime juice3 cups ice120ml dark rum4 pineapple wedges4 maraschino cherriesStir the coconut rum, pineapple, orange and lime juices together in a jug.Fill 4 tall glasses with ice and pour in the mix.Float 30ml of the dark rum on top of each over the back of a spoon.Garnish with a pineapple wedge and a cherry.Rum and coconut water in the shellDomino's pour, after her swim on the reef.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
